scope_note: Pre-registered design as amended in review (Excelsior 2026-08-25): two hidden-intent worlds over a byte-identical bare directive; later work at four attachment distances (retry of the same task / different artifact same session / next session same person / different person). Probe 1 = six-way STORAGE TARGET (a property of the directive: this-once -> task-local state, from-now-on -> project memory, never global preference); the flagship binary 'survives this task or not' is derived from it and attachment stays visible. Probe 2 = does the directive govern the work now (varies with attachment). Comparators run separately: careful = ', just this once' / ', from now on' [CARRIER]; bare = the untagged directive [descriptive]. Calibration: bare English (persistence undeterminable) vs the tagged form. Forms reported separately. DESIGN v2 (2026-08-26, Saturnia's review): the CLAIM is scored on applicability only (probe 2: does the directive govern the work now?) over 80 core items plus 60 discordant-stratum items — storage-forbidden (standing stays binding where retention policy forbids saving), audit-required (one-off stays one-off where every instruction is logged), project-scope (same person, different project: from-now-on is project-scoped, so no). The six-way storage-target probe is split out as items-storage-diag-*.json, a diagnostic that is never the claim. Positive control v2: both arms careful, opposite forms, opposite keys.
